client_brief:
Ironline Forge: editorial image set

Project overview
Ironline Forge casts bespoke iron and bronze for architects and developers who have mostly never stood on a foundry floor. We are hiring an expert to turn the supplied working files into Ironline Forge editorial image set and Ironline Forge color-continuity approval sheet.

What we will provide
ironline_floor_frames/ (14 frames, 4,000 to 4,600px long edge); ironline_maker_mark_casting.jpg; ironline_story_copy.txt. Every file must be accounted for in the final manifest; it may be used, retained as reference, superseded, or rejected with a reason.

Additional archive files
ironline_spec_card_2025.pdf; ironline_castings.csv. These files are supplied for provenance only because their former deliverable class is outside this commission. Do not silently turn them into extra scope.

Scope and deliverables
- Ironline Forge editorial image set: The shop-floor frames brought from two lighting conditions onto one base and then carried to a single committed dark tone with one hue, one strength and one grain across the set, straightened where the floor line rolled, every output at or below its source...
- Ironline Forge color-continuity approval sheet: A calibrated side-by-side approval sheet showing white point, black point, skin or material color, and crop consistency across the finished set. 

Non-negotiables
- Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
- Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
- Preserve identity, product geometry, material behavior, and documentary truth; retouching may improve presentation but may not change what the subject is.

Working process
Please begin with an inventory and risk pass, submit the first proof or direction at the stated checkpoint, then revise against consolidated feedback. We are hiring for judgment: flag contradictions early, make the strongest defensible choice, and document any source limitation rather than hiding it.

Contract
$1,800-$4,500 fixed; target delivery 2 to 4 weeks; one direction checkpoint and two consolidated revision rounds. Final handoff includes the delivery manifest, editable sources where scoped, final exports, and a concise production note.

source_provenance.statement: The scenario is synthesized from the repository's laundered Upwork and Freelancer source anchors. It is not represented as a verbatim live listing.
source_provenance.original_anchor: Ledger anchor for PHOTO-23, carrying both grounding notes the ledger holds. Upwork, quoted as far as the ledger carries it: 'Adapted from a real Upwork logo + challenge-coin vectorization brief (cand_38, db_i 95): the client already HAS hand-mocked concept art and needs it turned into polished, true vector artwork for a primary crest plus several symbolic coin-face designs, coin-ready and readable at small sizes, with versions that reproduce in flat black, reversed white, and struck gold and silver metal, deliverable as clean scalable vector plus product-ready exports for a mint/manufacturer handoff.' Freelancer.com, quoted as far as the ledger carries it: 'Adapted from a real Freelancer.com logo brief (the original asked for a mark in fully editable vector format (.ai or .eps), instantly readable at small sizes on labels and swing tags, print-ready CMYK output and scalable vector artwork, shipped with one-colour and reverse variants). Designing a NEW mark from scratch is out of Adobe-connector scope, so the doable, in-scope reading of that same requirement, take what the client actually has and turn it into clean, scalable, production-ready vector artwork plus the one-colour + reverse varia'. Absorbs AO-38 and AO-93. The verdict is REBUILD because the banked concept sat on the imaging surface alone and ended in a tinted set plus a traced mark, which is two deliverables. The fuller commission a foundry in this position genuinely buys, and the shape these are posted in, is the one built here: the mark recovered from the only artefact that carries it and proved at the sizes it will actually reproduce at, the editorial set committed to one tone, the stand panel and story page handed back editable because the next fair is in autumn, and the twelve casting spec cards reprinted off last year's press file. The foundry is the fictional Ironline Forge; no real firm, person, product or trademark is referenced.

price_band_and_audience: Heritage foundry selling bespoke architectural iron and bronze at five thousand to sixty thousand dollars a piece, to specifiers, architects and developers aged roughly 40 to 65 who are buying craft, permanence and the confidence that the piece will still be there in eighty years. The band is load-bearing throughout. At this level a committed dark single-tone editorial treatment is right because it sells process and provenance rather than product features: the buyer wants to believe there are people and heat behind the piece. Run the same job for a commodity fastener supplier and every choice inverts: that catalogue needs bright, literal, evenly lit product shots on white, and this treatment would read as pretension and misprice the offer badly. The band also governs the mark. A maker's mark struck into iron is proof of origin at this price, so it has to be recovered faithfully rather than tidied into a fashionable monoline, and it has to hold at the smallest place it appears, because a specifier reading a spec card is exactly the person the mark is meant to reassure. The collateral follows: generous type, plenty of black, numbers set plainly and honestly, nothing that reads as promotional. Bright, energetic, offer-shaped design here would tell an architect this is a supplier rather than a workshop. The ledger records the base concept at 900 to 1,800 dollars; this full trade-fair commission, with the mark recovery, the editable panels and the twelve-record card run, sits at 2,200 to 4,000 dollars fixed.

assets_supplied.name: ironline_floor_frames/ (14 frames, 4,000 to 4,600px long edge)
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Two afternoons on the shop floor." The pour, hand-finishing a bronze balustrade section, castings cooling on the sand, the pattern racks, the roller door and the yard.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Five of the fourteen are lit only by the furnace, so their entire tonal range is compressed into a narrow band of orange and, once mapped onto a single tone ramp, the castings stop separating from the sand floor around them. Separately, three of the handheld frames carry a slight roll in the shop-floor line that reads as level in a full frame and becomes obvious the moment a tall panel crop is struck from them.

assets_supplied.name: ironline_maker_mark_casting.jpg
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The bracket with our maker's mark struck into it. That is the only place it exists." A 4,200px frame of a sand-cast iron bracket photographed on the bench, the mark struck into the face inside a raised border ring.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The mark is struck into raw sand-cast iron, so its enclosed counters and the gap inside its border ring carry the same pitted grey as the face around them, with no colour and no medium of its own to name. A trace of it reads convincingly at full canvas and closes its counters solid at the size the mark actually reproduces on a spec card and reversed on the dark ground, and the border ring means a background removal returns a filled disc rather than a mark. There is no option on the tracing step to tune any of this.

assets_supplied.name: ironline_spec_card_2025.pdf
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Last year's spec card, the file the printer used." A real press PDF of a single-sided leave-behind card carrying the casting reference, the name, the alloy and finish line, the weight and lead-time line, and a photograph frame, printed and font-embedded.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The card shows four cleanly separated blocks and a picture, which says nothing about how many frames the conversion will actually produce. Worse, the mapping readout's account of the card's story omits one run entirely (the reference line) while keeping the line break that followed it, so the string still looks well formed and every character offset after that point is short by that run's length, and the validator returns VALID on the wrong offsets with no warnings at all.

assets_supplied.name: ironline_castings.csv
assets_supplied.visible_description: The twelve castings with reference, name, alloy, finish, weight, lead time and an image column naming the frame each card should carry.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two castings were never photographed on their own, so both rows name the same shop-floor frame, and two of the names run to two lines where last year's card carried one. The weight and lead-time columns are also typed inconsistently across the rows, which is a copy decision the agent has to make rather than anything a tool reports.

assets_supplied.visible_description: The brand story text, the stand panel headline and standfirst, the social caption, the dark ground the story page and panels use, and the delivered size of each placement including the physical dimensions of the stand panel.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What a mark struck into raw sand-cast iron actually yields as artwork, and whether it survives the two placements the client named. The mark has no ink and no colour of its own: it exists only as the difference between a struck impression and the pitted face around it, and that face carries the same grey inside the letterforms' enclosed counters and inside the border ring as it does outside them. The trace comes back reading convincingly at full canvas, which is the only size anyone would look at it by default, and at the size it reproduces on a spec card the counters have closed solid and the border ring has merged into the letterforms, and reversed on the dark panel ground it loses its remaining edge entirely. Nothing reports any of this. The tracing step takes no options at all, so there is no parameter to have set correctly; the only lever is the raster preparation, and which preparation is needed cannot be chosen until the failure has been seen at real size on the real ground.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it and care cannot pre-empt it. The trace's fidelity is a function of this casting's surface texture, this photograph's light and the selection that produced it. There is no measurement, no preview at delivered size and no parameter on the trace, so an agent that words the selection well and gets the polarity right still cannot know how much of the mark survives without tracing it and putting it on a spec card. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the mark is struck into the iron and that it has to work small and reversed out of the dark, which is a client naming their hardest placements and their standing requirement exactly as they would to a designer, and asking for a note about where it holds is a request for professional advice rather than a disclosure that the answer is known. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is to go back and make a different asset: re-prepare the raster so the impression carries a usable edge before tracing, aim the selection at a different property of the photograph, or accept that the traced mark is a large-format asset and build a different small-size lockup from it, after which the panel, the story page and the cards are re-composed around a mark of a different weight and minimum size.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-prepare the raster to strengthen the struck edge before tracing rather than trying to repair the trace, re-select on wording aimed at what actually distinguishes the impression in this frame, re-trace, strip the ground path and inject a viewBox again, then re-place at spec-card size and reversed on the dark ground rather than assuming the second attempt took. If it still will not hold small, decide and state what carries that placement instead, and re-author the canvases and the card around the mark's real minimum size.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Twelve spec cards go into the hands of specifiers with the foundry's hundred-year-old maker's mark reproduced as a solid grey blob, and the stand panel carries a mark that has disappeared into its own background, in front of the exact audience the mark exists to reassure.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What last year's card actually becomes as a merge template. Two things are unknowable until the conversion has run and the document has been opened. First, the four cleanly separated blocks on the printed card do not tell you how many text frames the conversion produces, and if they collapse into one continuous story then per-frame mapping does not exist and every field has to be placed by character offset inside a single story, which is a completely different mapping strategy. Second, the mapping readout's account of that story omits one run (the reference line) while keeping the line break that followed it, so the string it reports still looks well formed and every offset after that point is short by that run's length. The validator returns VALID on those wrong offsets with no warnings, and the prepare step reports that the placeholders were created successfully, while some of them silently never landed. Nothing in any tool response distinguishes a template with six live fields from one with four.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it. Frame granularity is a property of how the PDF was drawn and is not under the agent's control or knowable from the printed page, and whether the readout's story matches the document's story can only be established by comparing them, which is running the operation. Doing it carefully does not help, because the readout is the artefact that is wrong. (b) Nothing states it. The brief simply says here is last year's print file and the spreadsheet, which is a client handing over what they have. No asset note in the client's hands, no acceptance line and no earlier step names the omitted run or the frame count. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is to abandon the mapping strategy and rebuild it on a different basis, offsets computed from the document's own story rather than from the readout, or per-frame replacement if the frames turn out to exist, which is a different mapping rather than the same one re-submitted.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Download and unpack the round-tripped document, reconstruct the story by concatenating its content runs, recompute every offset against that string, rebuild the mapping with the corrected positions in the order the tool requires, prepare the template again and then re-export and search for each placeholder by name rather than trusting the success message. If the frames turned out to be fewer than the printed card suggests, redesign which field goes where before any of that.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Twelve leave-behind cards are printed for a trade fair with the casting reference and the lead time silently absent from every one of them, which is the only information a specifier actually needs in order to call, and every tool in the chain reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether a licensed installation frame can sit with the foundry's own photography under this treatment. Stock search returns a small CDN thumbnail, and the frame's true tonal range, its true black point and how much detail survives in its shadows only exist after it is licensed, downloaded at full resolution and carried under the committed tone. Because everything here maps onto a single hue ramp, colour is not what decides: a candidate joins or fails on luminance structure, and two frames that look equally dark and equally moody at 240 pixels can be a full stop apart once tinted, with one of them turning to a flat black field beside a set built on furnace light and hard speculars. The result is only visible with the licensed frame and the finished set laid out together.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it. The comparison needs both the licensed frame and the tinted set to exist, so it cannot be moved earlier, and it cannot be settled by care because a thumbnail carries no information about tonal range. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says only that they have no wide installation shot and to buy one if the panel needs it, which is an invitation carrying no claim about how a candidate will behave. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The likely response is to abandon the frame and search again on different terms, which is a new licensing decision, a new grade and a new judgement, or to resolve it instead by extending one of the foundry's own frames at its edges and accepting a different panel, which changes the panel's composition and the type that sits on it.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Push the licensed frame further under the tone, or, if it will not join, return to Stock with a search framed by the tonal structure the set actually has rather than by the subject matter, license a replacement and re-tint it, then lay the whole set out again and judge it as fifteen rather than checking the new frame on its own. If nothing joins, extend one of the foundry's own frames at its edges instead and re-compose the panel around the height that produces.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The tall panel at a trade fair stand, the largest thing the foundry will put in front of an architect all year, carries a bought photograph that visibly does not belong to the set beside it.

decision_gates: How dark and how committed the tone goes, given that at this band it has to read as a workshop rather than as a filter.
Whether both lighting conditions are brought onto one base before the tone is committed, or the tone is committed on top of two different bases.
Where a global correction stops working and the move has to be masked to a named material rather than to the object it belongs to, with molten metal and sand wanting opposite moves.
How to word a selection on a mark that has no ink and no colour, where the wording that lifts a printed mark off a substrate has nothing to grip.
Which raster preparation gives the struck impression a usable edge before tracing, given that the tracing step takes no options at all.
Whether the traced mark is a large-format asset only, and if so what carries the spec card and the reversed panel instead.
Which frames can carry the stand panel at its real physical size, and whether to crop tighter, extend at the edges or move the placement when a frame runs short.
What to do about the frames whose floor line rolls, given that the roll is invisible in a full frame and obvious in a tall crop.

why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns a foundry that does not exist and a mark that is not theirs. IDENTITY is the entire commission: the maker's mark is a specific impression cut into a specific die by a specific person's grandfather, struck into every piece the firm sells, and a regenerated version of it is another workshop's mark being passed off as proof of origin to specifiers buying on provenance. The photographs are of this building and these castings, and an architect will stand in front of the panel at the fair. SPEC: the deliverables are defined by numbers and surfaces a generation cannot satisfy, a mark that must be placeable scalable geometry with a real viewBox and no opaque ground path, a stand panel at true physical dimensions produced without inventing a pixel, and twelve cards at one record per page carrying the correct casting's photograph with every mapped field present. EDITABILITY: the panel set exists as a deliverable because the foundry changes it before the next fair, so it has to arrive as a native document with live text and real vector geometry rather than a flat picture of a layout. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: does this trace still read at the size a spec card reproduces it, does this template actually contain the fields the tools said it does, does this licensed frame join the set once both are tinted. None of that is a generation problem, and the honest note about where the mark will not hold is professional advice a render cannot give.
